newsitem.title: POLAND: Kredyt says interested in Warta issue.
newsitem.headline: Kredyt says interested in Warta issue.

text.p: Poland's Kredyt Bank SA is interested in taking up shares from the planned TUiR Warta SA new issue and establishing closer ties with the insurer, Kredyt's spokesman said.
"We certainly are considering such a possibility (of taking up Warta shares) and we would like to...establish closer cooperation with Warta," Marcin Olkowicz told Reuters.
On Thursday Warta announced a plan to offer up to 2.6 million new shares to Kredyt Bank, Bank Przemyslowo-Handlowy (BPH), Powszechny Bank Kredytowy SA (PBK) and two of its minority shareholders. @
Asked whether the new share issue could pave the way for a financial group, Olkowicz said it was too early for such speculation but that such an option could not be ruled out.
"I don't know whether it's not too early for an answer to such a question, but I don't deny such a possibility exists," he said.
Warta, whose shareholders are due to vote on the new issue on November 14, and the other two banks declined comment on the new issue and possible consolidation plans. @
Earlier this year, however PBK, Kredyt Bank and another listed bank, Polish Development Bank (PBR) moved ahead with creating equity links.
PBK has acquired a 25 percent stake in Kredyt Bank and is about to finalise an acquisition of almost 33 percent of PBR.
In turn PBR and Kredyt have said they wanted to buy significant stakes in PBK during its privatisation due by April 1997.
According to media reports based on banking sources, there were plans to create a financial group encompassing the three banks, BPH and Warta. @
So far only Kredyt Bank has mentioned Warta and BPH as possible partners but a source at one of the banks said there was a strong possibility that such a group would emerge.
"Such a group will be certainly developing because everything points that way," a banker, who asked not to be named, told Reuters.
